name: Kingdom of Herod Agrippa I
alt: Kingdom of Judea under Agrippa I

predecessors.name: Tetrarchy of Philip
predecessors.text: 'the old tetrarchies of Philip and Lysanias', given by Caligula in 37 (they had been added to the province of Syria after 34)

predecessors.name: Tetrarchy of Galilee and Peraea
predecessors.text: Antipas's domains, Galilee and Perea, after his exile in 39

predecessors.name: Roman Empire
predecessors.text: 'the former territories of Herod Archelaus' (Judea, Samaria and Idumea), given by Claudius in 41

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Judea became a Roman province under the procurator Cuspius Fadus; the northern lands are not followed by the page

ledger.x: 37: Caligula makes Agrippa king of the north.
37: Philip's former territories pass to Agrippa.
37: Agrippa is a Roman client king, made so by Caligula (page: Caligula 'granted him the title of king').
41: Claudius adds Judea, Samaria and Idumea.
44: Agrippa dies at Caesarea and the client kingdom ends.
44: Judea becomes a province under the procurator Cuspius Fadus.
44: the kingdom ends with the king's death.

certainty.note: No page gives boundaries; the districts of Philip and Antipas are stand-ins (Golan, Hauran, Galilee, Gilead).
